text: This is a garment factory thirty days before a buyer audit. Its fire safety certificate expires eleven days before the auditor arrives. One document, two failing requirements, and nobody has noticed yet.

Apparel and home textiles were 83.29 percent of Bangladesh's exports in fiscal year 2024 to 25. By June 2025, 800 of the 1,875 factories covered by the R M G Sustainability Council had completed structural remediation. The proof lives in scattered P D Fs, and gaps surface during the audit.

ThreadLight builds a Verified Evidence Passport. Every buyer requirement is linked to its evidence, every finding cites its source, and nothing is closed until a named person approves it. All data in this demo is synthetic.
Six documents. Extraction is shown as a pre-computed sample. The five rule stages run live in the browser.
In the evidence graph, one fire certificate supports two requirements. If it lapses, both fail together.

Each finding explains its status with a cited source. Integrity alerts flag records that disagree: committee minutes citing a certificate number that is not on file, and an emergency exit fix marked complete with no proof. They are prompts to check, not accusations.
What if the certificate is renewed? Coverage jumps from 29 to 55 percent. One day short of the audit, it drops back.

We assign the finding and upload the renewal. The rules recheck: both requirements are now pending human review, and coverage stays at 29. Can the system close it on its own? No. A named compliance officer approves, coverage rises to 55, and the officer closes it.
The report separates verified from open items, in English or Bangla. It is a draft for human review, not an audit result.

How does it decide? Rules decide dates, coverage and status. Models only read text. Every finding is cited, and people approve every closure. Today, the rules engine, graph, what-if, approval loop and bilingual report are implemented and tested. O C R, language model extraction and drafting are planned next.
We are looking for pilot factories and advisors who know garment compliance. ThreadLight: evidence you can verify, before the auditor asks.
